title: Fewest clues
description: Add k clues to a partly filled 4 x 4 Sudoku so that it has exactly one solution; the fewest clues problem is Sigma-2-complete (Demaine, Ma, Schvartzman, Waingarten and Aaronson). The abstraction guesses a solved grid and the cells to reveal; the check looks for two different grids that agree with all clues, and the refinement adds a clue that rules out one of them. Delete the printed clues and raise k for larger runs.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The size of the puzzle and the printed clues. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% A 4 x 4 Sudoku: every row, every column and each of the four 2 x 2 boxes contains the
% values 1..4 once. The printed clues pre(R,C,V) are in the Instances tab.
row(1..4). col(1..4). val(1..4).
box(R,C,(R-1)/2*2+(C-1)/2) :- row(R), col(C).
printed(R,C) :- pre(R,C,_).

fragments.name: sudoku
fragments.description: The rules of the puzzle for any grid; used by solver A (one grid) and solver C (two grids).
fragments.text:
% The rules of the puzzle, for every grid G that a solver declares with grid(G):
% cell(G,R,C,V) says that grid G has the value V in row R, column C.
1 { cell(G,R,C,V) : val(V) } 1 :- grid(G), row(R), col(C).
:- cell(G,R,C1,V), cell(G,R,C2,V), C1 < C2.
:- cell(G,R1,C,V), cell(G,R2,C,V), R1 < R2.
:- cell(G,R1,C1,V), cell(G,R2,C2,V), box(R1,C1,B), box(R2,C2,B), (R1,C1) < (R2,C2).
% Every grid respects the printed clues.
:- grid(G), pre(R,C,V), not cell(G,R,C,V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a solved grid and k of its cells as clues.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a solved grid s and k of its cells that are revealed as clues.
grid(s).
k { clue(R,C) : row(R), col(C), not printed(R,C) } k.
% given(R,C,V): the puzzle shows the value V in row R, column C.
given(R,C,V) :- clue(R,C), cell(s,R,C,V).
#show given/3.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the clues with their values. The solved grid stays private to solver A.
fragments.text: glue(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for two different grids that agree with all clues (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: two different grids a and b that both agree with the clues.
% (One of them may be the candidate's own grid.)
grid(a). grid(b).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(a,R,C,V).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
differ :- cell(a,R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
:- not differ.
#show.
#show a(R,C,V) : cell(a,R,C,V).
#show b(R,C,V) : cell(b,R,C,V).

% Both grids fit every puzzle that shows only values on which they agree. So a clue
% has to appear that contradicts one of them: any value in a cell where a or b has
% another value.
both(R,C,V) :- cell(a,R,C,V), cell(b,R,C,V).
relevant(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C), not both(R,C,V).

fragments.name: check_close
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: two different grids a and b that both agree with the clues.
% (One of them may be the candidate's own grid.)
grid(a). grid(b).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(a,R,C,V).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
differ :- cell(a,R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
:- not differ.
#show.
#show a(R,C,V) : cell(a,R,C,V).
#show b(R,C,V) : cell(b,R,C,V).

% Both grids fit every puzzle that shows only values on which they agree. So a clue
% has to appear that contradicts one of them: any value in a cell where a or b has
% another value.
both(R,C,V) :- cell(a,R,C,V), cell(b,R,C,V).
relevant(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C), not both(R,C,V).
% Variant closest-pair: two grids that differ in as few cells as possible give the
% shortest clause (with 'optimal').
#minimize { 1,R,C,V : relevant(given(R,C,V)) }.
fragments.description: The check that prefers close pairs of grids, for the variant closest-pair.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction
solver C = shared + sudoku + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% Clues that are already printed in the grid.
pre(1,1,1). pre(2,2,2).

% The same printed clues with k = 1: one more clue never makes the solution
% unique.
pre(1,1,1). pre(2,2,2).

% Three printed clues on the diagonal, and one more clue (k = 1).
pre(1,1,1). pre(2,2,2). pre(3,3,3).

% The first row is printed; two more clues (k = 2).
pre(1,1,1). pre(1,2,2). pre(1,3,3). pre(1,4,4).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction
solver C = shared + sudoku + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction
solver C = shared + sudoku + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction
solver C = shared + sudoku + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three pairs of grids per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + sudoku + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction
solver C = shared + sudoku + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

generators.name: printed
generators.description: m printed clues of a random 4 x 4 Sudoku grid (a fixed grid with its rows, columns and values permuted).
generators.text:
% printed: a random solved 4 x 4 grid (rows swapped within bands, columns within stacks, values permuted), m of its cells printed
base(R,C,((R-1)\2*2+(R-1)/2+C-1)\4+1) :- R = 1..4, C = 1..4.
rmap(R,(R-1)/2*2+@perm(2, (R-1)\2+1, rows, (R-1)/2)) :- R = 1..4.
cmap(C,(C-1)/2*2+@perm(2, (C-1)\2+1, cols, (C-1)/2)) :- C = 1..4.
full(R2,C2,@perm(4, V, vals)) :- base(R,C,V), rmap(R,R2), cmap(C,C2).
pre(R,C,V) :- full(R,C,V), @subset(m, 16, (R-1)*4+C, cells) = 1.
#show pre/3.

readme:
# Project: fewest clues on 4 × 4 Sudoku

## Research question

The fewest clues problem is Σ2P-complete. How does the number of candidates grow with the number of clues to add (k) and with the number of printed clues?

## Baseline

64 solutions (exhausted) after 353 candidates and 289 clauses, 0.5 s, at k = 2 on the example instance.

## Things to try

- A suite over k (a constants grid) and over the instances; fit the growth factor per step of k.
- A refinement that names the whole unavoidable set (as in `sudoku-unavoidable`) instead of one clue.
- Write a generator of partly filled grids and look for the hardest ones (Fuzz, mining).

## How to measure

Add the variants, write a suite over the instances (Campaign tab, Advanced mode), and read the instance × variant matrix; headless: `node tools/bench.mjs <id> --suite NAME --out rows.jsonl` and `node tools/report.mjs rows.jsonl`. Check every variant against the `reference` loop (or the audit) on small instances before trusting its numbers.
